column1: The unique conditions for expanding the theme of "light diffraction" in everyday physical scenarios are as follows: color change of the light source, introduction of diffraction obstacles of different shapes, periodic variation in the intensity of the light source, addition of reflective surfaces in the diffraction path, addition of transparent filtering materials in the diffraction path, observing diffraction at the boundaries between different media, placing the diffracting object in a fluid and moving it, using multiple light sources to diffract simultaneously, rotating or vibrating the diffraction screen, introducing refractive media in the diffraction path, projecting the light source at different angles, using moving obstacles in the diffraction path, adding lenses or prisms in the diffraction path, observing changes by altering the size and shape of the diffracting object, introducing symmetrical or asymmetrical structures in the diffraction path. These conditions aim to enrich the complexity or diversity of "light diffraction" scenarios in a macroscopically observable and visualized manner.
